sentences.zh: 历史一直是一部关于权力的故事。

sentences.en: Who seeks it?
sentences.zh: 谁在寻求权力？

sentences.en: Who seizes it?
sentences.zh: 谁在夺取权力？

sentences.en: And how easily it can all slip away.
sentences.zh: 而这一切又是多么容易转瞬即逝。

sentences.en: The Caesars, the Caliphs, the Tsars, they conquered vast swathes of the world.
sentences.zh: 恺撒、哈里发、沙皇，他们曾征服了广袤的世界。

sentences.en: They proclaimed themselves the favorites of the gods, and yet their empires crumbled away.
sentences.zh: 他们自诩为神明的宠儿，然而他们的帝国终究分崩离析。

sentences.en: It is easier to conquer than it is to control.
sentences.zh: 征服容易，掌控难。

sentences.zh: Hive 采取了不同的方法。

sentences.en: It puts power where it belongs, in your hands.
sentences.zh: 它将权力放在它本该属于的地方——你的手中。

sentences.en: Checking your phone, seeing the heating's on, the cars charging, and the sun is quietly earning its keep on the roof.
sentences.zh: 查看手机，看到暖气开着，汽车正在充电，而阳光正静静地在屋顶上创造价值。

sentences.zh: 访问 HiveHome.com 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: I speak to you for the first time as Prime Minister, in a solemn hour for the life of our country, of our empire, of our allies, and above all, of the cause of freedom.
sentences.zh: 我今天第一次以首相身份向你们发表讲话，在这个庄严的时刻，为了我们国家、我们的帝国、我们的盟友的生命，最重要的是，为了自由的事业。

sentences.en: A tremendous battle is raging in France and Flanders.
sentences.zh: 一场激烈的战斗正在法国和法兰德斯肆虐。

sentences.en: The Germans, by a remarkable combination of air-bombing and heavily armoured tanks, have broken through the French defences north of the Maginot Line.
sentences.zh: 德国人通过空中轰炸和重型装甲坦克的惊人组合，突破了马奇诺防线以北的法国防御。

sentences.en: If this is one of the most awe-struck, in the long history of France and Britain, it is also beyond doubt the most sublime, side by side, unaided,
sentences.zh: 如果说这是法国和英国漫长历史上最令人敬畏的时刻，那它也无疑是最崇高的，并肩作战，孤军奋战，

sentences.en: except by their kith and kin in the great dominions, and by the wide empires which rest beneath their shield.
sentences.zh: 除了伟大的自治领中的同胞至亲，以及庇护在他们盾牌之下的广袤帝国之外，别无外援。

sentences.en: Side by side, the British and French peoples have advanced to rescue not only Europe, but mankind, from the foulest and most soul-destroying tyranny,
sentences.zh: 英国和法国人民并肩作战，不仅是为了拯救欧洲，也是为了拯救全人类，使其免受有史以来最黑暗、最摧残灵魂的暴政的荼毒，

sentences.en: which has ever darkened and stained the pages of history.
sentences.zh: 那暴政曾令历史的篇章黯然失色、污点斑斑。

sentences.en: Behind them, behind us, behind the armies and fleets of Britain and France.
sentences.zh: 在他们身后，在我们身后，在英国和法国的陆海军身后。

sentences.en: Gather a group of shattered states and bludgeoned races.
sentences.zh: 汇聚了一群支离破碎的国家和饱受摧残的种族。

sentences.en: The Czechs, the Poles, the Norwegians, the Danes, the Dutch, the Belgians.
sentences.zh: 捷克人、波兰人、挪威人、丹麦人、荷兰人、比利时人。

sentences.en: Upon all of whom the long night of barbarism will descend, unbroken even by a star of hope.
sentences.zh: 漫长的野蛮之夜将降临在他们所有人身上，甚至连一颗希望之星都不会划破黑暗。

sentences.en: Unless we conquer, as conquer we muSt.
sentences.zh: 除非我们征服，正如我们必须征服的那样。

sentences.en: As conquer we shall.
sentences.zh: 正如我们必将征服那样。

sentences.en: So that, Dominic, it will stun you to learn, was a Winston Churchill, and it was his first radio address as British Prime Minister, delivered on the 19th of May, 1940.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，你可能会大吃一惊，那是温斯顿·丘吉尔，这是他作为英国首相的首次电台广播，发表于 1940 年 5 月 19 日。

sentences.en: And when he gave that address, he had been Prime Minister for only nine days, but never in history.
sentences.zh: 当他发表那次演讲时，他担任首相才仅仅九天，但历史上从未有过。

sentences.en: Had anybody taken office against quite such a bleak backdrop.
sentences.zh: 任何人是在如此黯淡的背景下接任这一职务的。

sentences.en: So we ended our previous episode with Hitler preparing his great attack in the West,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在上一集的结尾讲到希特勒正准备他在西方的重大进攻，

sentences.en: an attack that huge numbers of people in the German high command thought was a disastrous policy.
sentences.zh: 德军最高指挥部里有大量的人认为这场进攻是一项灾难性的政策。

sentences.en: But actually, in the short term, Hitler had been proved right because the blow fell on the Western armies on the 10th of May, the very day that Churchill had become Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，在短期内，事实证明希特勒是对的，因为就在丘吉尔成为首相的当天——也就是 5 月 10 日，打击落在了西方军队头上。

sentences.en: And what happens next is one of the great duels, one of the great dramas, not just in European, but all world history.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情是欧洲乃至整个世界历史上最伟大的决斗、最伟大的戏剧之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this week we're exploring the great turning point in the story of the Nazis, the events of 1940.
sentences.zh: 所以本周我们要探讨纳粹历史上一个伟大的转折点，即 1940 年的事件。

sentences.en: But let's just remind ourselves where we ended last time.
sentences.zh: 但让我们先回顾一下上期节目结束时我们讲到了哪里。

sentences.en: So Hitler in late 1939 crushed Poland, divided it with Stalin.
sentences.zh: 希特勒在 1939 年底粉碎了波兰，并与斯大林瓜分了它。

sentences.en: He has escaped a possible coup by his own generals.
sentences.zh: 他躲过了自己将军们可能发动的政变。

sentences.en: He's also escaped a bomb attack in a Munich beer hall.
sentences.zh: 他还躲过了慕尼黑一家啤酒馆里的炸弹袭击。

sentences.en: And he has told his high command to prepare an attack on France and England, as he calls it, at the earliest and most favourable moment.
sentences.zh: 并且他已经指示他的最高指挥部，在最早且最有利的时机，准备对法兰西和英格兰（他这么称呼）发起进攻。

sentences.en: And that attack has been much postponed and timetabled for the spring of 1940.
sentences.zh: 那场进攻曾被多次推迟，并被排期到了 1940 年的春天。

sentences.en: And we'll be coming to that attack and to Churchill's emergence as Britain's saviour later in this episode.
sentences.zh: 我们将在本集的后面部分讲到那场进攻以及丘吉尔作为英国救世主的崛起。

sentences.en: But first, somewhere we haven't discussed at all in the whole of this series on the Third Reich, going back four seasons, and that is the North.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我们要去一个在前四季的整个第三帝国系列中完全没有讨论过的地方，那就是北方。

sentences.en: And the irony being that the Nazis were so obsessed with their northern inheritance and their kind of their Nordic roots and Norse myths,
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，纳粹如此痴迷于他们的北方传承以及某种北欧根源和北欧神话，

sentences.en: but they never gave much thought to Scandinavia, really.
sentences.zh: 但他们其实从来没有对斯堪的纳维亚给予太多关注。

sentences.en: But we mentioned the iron ore in Sweden, which I'm very excited about.
sentences.zh: 不过我们提到了瑞典的铁矿石，这让我非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Yes, and that will come.
sentences.zh: 是的，这后面会讲到。

sentences.en: But also, you touched on Finland, didn't you?
sentences.zh: 而且，你还提到了芬兰，不是吗？

sentences.en: The fact that the Soviets were bogged down in the snows of that distant northern land.
sentences.zh: 苏联人深陷于那个遥远北方国度的冰天雪地之中。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like listening to Winston Churchill.
sentences.zh: 是的，这感觉就像在听温斯顿·丘吉尔说话。

sentences.en: I know, I'm kind of infected by it.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我有点被他感染了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The brave people of Finland.
sentences.zh: 勇敢的芬兰人民。

sentences.en: So Finland, formerly the Grand Duchy of Finland, had been part of the Russian Empire, three and a half million people.
sentences.zh: 芬兰以前是芬兰大公国，曾是俄罗斯帝国的一部分，拥有三百五十万人口。

sentences.en: And Stalin had attacked it at the end of November 1939 because he had given an ultimatum to the Finns to hand over a chunk of Karelia,
sentences.zh: 斯大林在 1939 年 11 月底发动了对芬兰的进攻，因为他曾向芬兰人发出最后通牒，要求割让卡累利阿的一部分，

sentences.en: the bitter Finland that is just above Leningrad, formerly St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 也就是紧邻列宁格勒（原圣彼得堡）的那片饱受冰雪摧残的芬兰土地。

sentences.en: The Finns, to his great surprise, said no.
sentences.zh: 令斯大林大跌眼镜的是，芬兰人说不。

sentences.en: Stalin sent in the Red Army.
sentences.zh: 斯大林派出了红军。

sentences.en: But the Red Army was useless at this stage because Stalin had killed all their generals as part of the Great Terror.
sentences.zh: 但当时的红军毫无用处，因为斯大林在大清洗中杀掉了他们所有的将军。

sentences.en: He had purged them.
sentences.zh: 他清洗了他们。

sentences.en: And they were completely unprepared.
sentences.zh: 而且他们完全没有准备。

sentences.en: We think of the Russians as supremely well-equipped to fight in the winter.
sentences.zh: 我们认为俄国人极其擅长在冬天下作战。

sentences.en: But they were very unprepared compared with the Finns, who were wearing these kind of white camouflage uniforms and were on skis and were throwing Molotov cocktails at them.
sentences.zh: 但与芬兰人相比，他们毫无准备，芬兰人穿着这种白色迷彩服，踩着滑雪板，向他们投掷莫洛托夫鸡尾酒（燃烧瓶）。

sentences.en: So that this is the war that gives us the Molotov cocktail.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那个诞生了莫洛托夫鸡尾酒的战争。

sentences.en: And basically, Finland is clearly never going to completely win the war because it's tiny compared with the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，芬兰显然永远不可能彻底赢得这场战争，因为它和苏联比起来实在是太渺小了。

sentences.en: Basically, the two sides had to agree a compromise.
sentences.zh: 基本上，双方不得不达成妥协。

sentences.en: And in March 1940, the Finns handed over a chunk of Karelia.
sentences.zh: 1940 年 3 月，芬兰人割让了一部分卡累利阿。

sentences.en: But Stalin then dropped his previous plan of basically turning Finland into a semi-absorbed client state.
sentences.zh: 但斯大林随后放弃了他先前的计划，即把芬兰变成一个半吸收的附庸国的计划。

sentences.en: And he lets them keep their independence.
sentences.zh: 他让他们保持了独立。

sentences.en: And the result of this war, the Winter War, is that the Red Army have lost about 125,000 men killed.
sentences.zh: 这场战争（即冬季战争）的结果是，红军大约有 12.5 万人战死。

sentences.en: And another 300,000 have been incapacitated by wounds or they've basically got disease or they've got frostbites.
sentences.zh: 另有 30 万人因伤丧失战斗力，或者基本上染上了疾病，或者冻伤。

sentences.en: And Hitler's been watching this, right?
sentences.zh: 希特勒一直在关注这件事，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so he thinks, ah, this demonstrates that the Soviet Army is rubbish and therefore it will be easy for us to conquer it.
sentences.zh: 所以他认为，啊，这证明了苏联军队是个垃圾，因此我们征服它易如反掌。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: It's really important, actually, in Hitler's thinking, this so-called Winter War between Finland and the USSR.
sentences.zh: 在希特勒的思想中，这场所谓的芬兰与苏联之间的冬季战争实际上非常重要。

sentences.en: Because Hitler, as he says to his top brass, we have only to kick in the door and the whole rotten structure of the Soviet Union will come crashing down.
sentences.zh: 因为正如希特勒对他的高级将领们所说，我们只需踹开大门，苏联这整个腐朽的架构就会轰然倒塌。

sentences.en: And this is what everybody believes, having watched what happened in Finland.
sentences.zh: 在目睹了芬兰发生的事情之后，所有人都是这么认为的。

sentences.en: Now, Finland is therefore preserved as a buffer in the north between Scandinavia and the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 因此，芬兰作为北方斯堪的纳维亚与苏联之间的缓冲区被保留了下来。

sentences.en: And so now Hitler can work on a plan to bring Scandinavia into his empire.
sentences.zh: 所以现在希特勒可以着手制定一个将斯堪的纳维亚纳入其帝国的计划了。

sentences.en: And the key thing here, which I know is something that really excites you, is iron ore.
sentences.zh: 这里关键的一点——我知道这也是让你非常兴奋的事情——就是铁矿石。

sentences.en: There's nothing I enjoy more than a discussion about iron ore.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比讨论铁矿石更让我高兴的了。

sentences.en: Can I give you some stats?
sentences.zh: 能让我报一些数据吗？

sentences.en: I'd love an iron ore statistic.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意听铁矿石的数据。

sentences.en: So, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And listeners, here is some exciting iron ore stats.
sentences.zh: 还有各位听众，这里有一些令人兴奋的铁矿石数据。

sentences.en: And they come from the war in the West by my brother, James Holland.
sentences.zh: 它们来自我兄弟詹姆斯·霍兰德所著的《西方战争》。

sentences.en: By December 1939, British intelligence deduced that of the 22 million tons of iron ore imported in 1938,
sentences.zh: 截至 1939 年 12 月，英国情报机构推断，在 1938 年进口的 2200 万吨铁矿石中，

sentences.en: the equivalent of nine and a half million tons of that supply had come from sources now close to it.
sentences.zh: 相当于 950 万吨的供应量来自目前受到威胁的来源。

sentences.en: And so that is obviously a massive crisis for the Nazi war effort, because without iron ore, they can't build their planes and guns and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 因此，这对纳粹的战争努力显然是一场巨大的危机，因为没有铁矿石，他们就无法制造飞机、枪支以及所有这类东西。

sentences.en: And so that puts an absolute premium on the one remaining guaranteed source of iron ore, and that is Sweden.
sentences.zh: 所以这就把唯一剩下的有保障的铁矿石来源——也就是瑞典——推到了绝对至关重要的地位。

sentences.en: So you can see why this is a huge kind of determinant in Nazi war planning.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出为什么这是纳粹战争规划中一个巨大的决定性因素。

sentences.en: Massive.
sentences.zh: 巨大的。

sentences.en: It's absolutely massive.
sentences.zh: 绝对是巨大的。

sentences.en: Isn't that interesting?
sentences.zh: 这难道不有趣吗？

sentences.en: I think that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: It's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: I think it's probably the most fascinating fact we ever have on the rest of this history.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能是我们在这段历史中遇到的最吸引人的事实了。

sentences.en: Anyway, so this iron ore is produced by mines in the north of Sweden.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这些铁矿石是由瑞典北部的矿山开采的。

sentences.en: It comes out of Sweden through one port in particular, which is Narvik, across the border in northern Norway.
sentences.zh: 它从瑞典运出，特别通过一个港口，那就是位于挪威北部边境的纳尔维克。

sentences.en: Which I think is a great name, Narvik.
sentences.zh: 我觉得纳尔维克这个名字真棒。

sentences.en: Yeah, I've been to Narvik, actually.
sentences.zh: 对，我其实去过纳尔维克。

sentences.en: Have you?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Kind of nondescript.
sentences.zh: 有点平淡无奇。

sentences.en: But a good name.
sentences.zh: 但名字不错。

sentences.en: Yeah, but a good name.
sentences.zh: 对，但名字不错。

sentences.en: So Narvik is also ice-free in winter, so you can bring iron ore all year round.
sentences.zh: 所以纳尔维克在冬天也是不冻港，因此你可以全年运送铁矿石。

sentences.en: Now, as soon as the war broke out in September 1939, Grand Admiral Rader of the Kriegsmarine, which is the navy, went to Hitler and said,
sentences.zh: 现在，一到 1939 年 9 月战争爆发，德国海军（Kriegsmarine）总司令雷德尔海军元帅就去找希特勒说，

sentences.en: look, we have to guarantee this flow of iron ore from northern Sweden.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们必须确保来自瑞典北部的铁矿石源源不断。

sentences.en: In other words, we have to establish ourselves in Norway, which is neutral, because if we don't, the Allies will.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们必须在中立的挪威建立我们的势力，因为如果我们不这样做，盟军就会这么做。

sentences.en: And if they get there first, we're in real trouble.
sentences.zh: 如果他们先到那里，我们就大难临头了。

sentences.en: And Rader said to Hitler, this business of the winter war in Finland is a real issue, because the Allies, I think, will use that as a pretext.
sentences.zh: 雷德尔对希特勒说，芬兰冬季战争这件事是个真正的问题，因为我认为盟军会把它当作借口。

sentences.en: They will send troops to help Finland against Stalin, and on the way, they will occupy Norway and northern Sweden.
sentences.zh: 他们会派军队去帮芬兰对抗斯大林，顺便他们会占领挪威和瑞典北部。

sentences.en: And the thing is, he's right, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 问题是，他说得对，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because actually, the Allies do have exactly such a plan.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，盟军确实有这样一个计划。

sentences.en: They do, and this may surprise a lot of listeners.
sentences.zh: 他们确实有，这可能会让很多听众感到惊讶。

sentences.en: The Allies absolutely had such a plan.
sentences.zh: 盟军绝对有这样一个计划。

sentences.en: Churchill, now running the Admiralty, the navy in Britain, is especially keen on it.
sentences.zh: 目前在英国海军部掌权的海军大臣丘吉尔对这个计划尤为热心。

sentences.en: So under his aegis, Britain and France draw up a plan to invade Denmark and Norway.
sentences.zh: 因此在他的庇护下，英国和法国制定了一项入侵丹麦和挪威的计划。

sentences.en: Basically, if you're invading Norway, you have to take Denmark as well, because it's right next door.
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果你要入侵挪威，你也必须占领丹麦，因为它就在隔壁。

sentences.en: They would have landed troops at Narvik.
sentences.zh: 他们本会在纳尔维克登陆军队。

sentences.en: They would have seized the Swedish iron mines, and they would have then pushed troops further on into Finland to help the Finns against Stalin, who at this point,
sentences.zh: 他们本会夺取瑞典的铁矿，然后他们会把军队进一步推进到芬兰，以帮助芬兰人对抗斯大林，当时斯大林在他们看来，

sentences.en: they kind of perceive as Hitler's ally, his partner in crime.
sentences.zh: 有点像是希特勒的盟友，他的犯罪同伙。

sentences.en: Now, they ended up scrapping this plan, basically in part because the Norwegians and the Swedes got wind of it.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们最终废弃了这个计划，部分原因是因为挪威人和瑞典人风闻了此事。

sentences.en: And they said, what?
sentences.zh: 他们说，什么？

sentences.en: You're planning to occupy us?
sentences.zh: 你们打算占领我们？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's not good, is it?
sentences.zh: 对，这可不太妙，对吧？

sentences.en: That's outrageous.
sentences.zh: 这太离谱了。

sentences.en: But the threat is still there.
sentences.zh: 但威胁依然存在。

sentences.en: So on the 20th of February, Hitler summoned one of his generals, who was called Paul von Falkenhorst, and said, I want you to come up with a plan to invade Norway and Denmark.
sentences.zh: 因此，在 2 月 20 日，希特勒召见了他的一个名叫保罗·冯·法肯霍斯特的将军，并说，我要你拿出个入侵挪威和丹麦的计划。

sentences.en: And this is a very good indication of the mad way that Hitler does business.
sentences.zh: 这很好地说明了希特勒那疯狂的行事方式。

sentences.en: It's so funny.
sentences.zh: 太搞笑了。

sentences.en: So he calls to this guy, Falkenhorst, and says, and by the way, I need this plan.
sentences.zh: 所以他把这个叫法肯霍斯特的家伙叫来，然后说，顺便说一句，我需要这个计划。

sentences.en: You've got until five o'clock this afternoon.
sentences.zh: 你今天下午五点之前必须交出来。

sentences.en: I don't know what time it is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道当时是几点。

sentences.en: It's like lunchtime or something.
sentences.zh: 大概是午饭时间或者别的什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, kind of three hours.
sentences.zh: 对，大约有三个小时。

sentences.en: And also, you can't tell anyone about it, and you can't get any help.
sentences.zh: 而且，你不能把这件事告诉任何人，你也不能寻求任何帮助。

sentences.en: So he goes to a bookshop, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他去了一家书店，对吧？

sentences.en: He gets a Beideker, a guide to Scandinavia.
sentences.zh: 他买了一本贝德克尔指南，一本关于斯堪的纳维亚的旅游指南。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he books himself into a hotel, Falkenhorst, with this guidebook, and sort of in desperation, he hasn't even got any maps or anything.
sentences.zh: 法肯霍斯特带着这本旅游指南给自己订了一个酒店房间，带着一种绝望的心情，他甚至连地图都没有。

sentences.en: He's just got a guidebook, desperately scribbling, I don't know, in hotel notepaper or something, the plan to invade Norway and Denmark.
sentences.zh: 他只有一个旅游指南，绝望地在酒店信纸上或其他什么东西上胡乱涂写着入侵挪威和丹麦的计划。

sentences.en: Hitler was convinced this would be very easy.
sentences.zh: 希特勒坚信这会非常容易。

sentences.en: And by the end of March, Grand Admiral Raider has said, come on, we need to hurry up.
sentences.zh: 到了三月底，雷德尔海军元帅说，得了吧，我们得抓紧了。

sentences.en: They set the date for the 9th of April.
sentences.zh: 他们把日期定在了4月9日。

sentences.en: Now, in the meantime, they obviously need a reason to go in, and ideally, they will have a local collaborator.
sentences.zh: 当然，在此期间，他们显然需要一个入侵的理由，最好能有一个当地的内应。

sentences.en: And Raider, the admiral, says to Hitler, look, I've got the perfect person.
sentences.zh: 雷德尔，这位海军元帅对希特勒说，听着，我找到了绝佳的人选。

sentences.en: There's this bloke from Norway.
sentences.zh: 挪威有个家伙。

sentences.en: He runs a fascist party called the National Samling.
sentences.zh: 他领导着一个名叫“国家团结”的法西斯政党。

sentences.en: I think, I don't know how my Norwegian pronunciation is.
sentences.zh: 我想，我不知道我的挪威语发音准不准。

sentences.en: And this bloke's name is Vidcon Quisling.
sentences.zh: 这家伙名叫吉斯林，维德孔·吉斯林。

sentences.en: And Quisling, you'll be delighted to hear this, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你听了准会高兴。

sentences.en: He's the son of a Lutheran pastor.
sentences.zh: 他是一个路德宗牧师的儿子。

sentences.en: Surely everybody in Norway is the son of a Lutheran pastor.
sentences.zh: 敢情挪威人个个都是路德宗牧师的儿子呗。

sentences.en: At least 30%, I would guess.
sentences.zh: 我猜至少有百分之三十。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He'd got the highest marks in the history of the Norwegian military academy, this bloke, Quisling.
sentences.zh: 这个叫吉斯林的家伙，拿过挪威军事学院历史上的最高分。

sentences.en: And he'd worked very closely with the explorer-turned-refugee campaigner, Fritjof Nansen.
sentences.zh: 而且他曾与探险家转型的难民活动家弗里德约夫·南森紧密合作。

sentences.en: Anyway, there's only about 10 people in Norway.
sentences.zh: 话说回来，挪威总共也就十来个人。

sentences.en: So if you've got those high marks in the academy, you can thrive in Norwegian politics.
sentences.zh: 所以在军校拿了高分，你就能在挪威政坛混得风生水起。

sentences.en: So Quisling was defence minister very briefly.
sentences.zh: 所以吉斯林曾短暂担任过国防大臣。

sentences.en: Then in the 1930s, he sort of got really into Nordic nationalism and he formed his own Nazi-style party.
sentences.zh: 然后在20世纪30年代，他迷上了北欧民族主义，并组建了自己的纳粹风格政党。

sentences.en: And he called himself the Führer of this party, spelt in an entertaining Norwegian way.
sentences.zh: 他自封为该党元首，这个词带有好玩的挪威拼写方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So it's a no with a dash through it.
sentences.zh: 也就是字母o上面划了一道杠。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But he never did well.
sentences.zh: 但他从来没混出什么名堂。

sentences.en: They were very poor.
sentences.zh: 他们穷得很。

sentences.en: They never got more than two and a half percent of the vote.
sentences.zh: 得票率从来没超过百分之二点五。

sentences.en: So that's what, about six people voting for?
sentences.zh: 那算什么，也就大约六个人投票吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And they never managed to elect a single Norwegian MP.
sentences.zh: 而且他们从未成功选出一名挪威议员。

sentences.en: Anyway, Rader brings him to Hitler and introduces him to Hitler, this guy Quisling.
sentences.zh: 总之，雷德尔把这个名叫吉斯林的家伙带去见希特勒，并把他引荐给希特勒。

sentences.en: And Hitler thinks that he's a bit useless.
sentences.zh: 而希特勒觉得他挺废物。

sentences.en: However, he's the only person they've got.
sentences.zh: 不过，这是他们唯一能用的人了。

sentences.en: So they decide to back him anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以他们还是决定支持他。

sentences.en: And Quisling does turn out to be genuinely useful to the Germans because he was defence minister.
sentences.zh: 而且吉斯林对德国人来说确实挺有用，因为他当过国防大臣。

sentences.en: So he's able to give them details of all Norway's defences.
sentences.zh: 所以他能提供挪威所有防御设施的详细信息。

sentences.en: So overt treason.
sentences.zh: 赤裸裸的叛国行为。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全是。

sentences.en: I mean, he really is a Quisling.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他真的是个地地道道的“吉斯林”（卖国贼）。

sentences.en: And, of course, that's where the name comes from.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是这个词的由来。

sentences.en: Now, in the meantime, the Allies, finally, unbelievable, they've actually got their act together and decided to do something.
sentences.zh: 话说回来，与此同时，盟军终于——简直难以置信——他们总算行动起来，决定做点什么了。

sentences.en: So the French have finally got rid of their dithering prime minister, who was Deladier, a socialiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以法国人终于赶走了他们优柔寡断的首相、身为社会主义者的达拉第。

sentences.en: And they've replaced him with somebody from the other end of the political spectrum, the centre-right, Paul Reynaud.
sentences.zh: 并换上了政治光谱另一端、中右翼的保罗·雷诺。

sentences.en: And Reynaud is a very clever man, kind of, you know, very impressive in many ways.
sentences.zh: 雷诺是个非常聪明的人，怎么说呢，在很多方面都令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: He's extremely short, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实他非常矮。

sentences.en: He's five foot three.
sentences.zh: 他身高只有五尺三寸。

sentences.en: So that's his defining characteristic.
sentences.zh: 这就是他最标志性的特征。

sentences.en: And he, Deladier, people used to say of Deladier, he made no decisions at all.
sentences.zh: 人们以前常说达拉第，说他什么决定都不做。

sentences.en: But Reynaud makes a decision every five minutes.
sentences.zh: 但雷诺每五分钟就要做一个决定。

sentences.en: And a lot of them are mad.
sentences.zh: 而且其中很多决定都极其疯狂。

sentences.en: So he's very like Churchill.
sentences.zh: 所以他真的很像丘吉尔。

sentences.en: He loves kind of mad invasions of remote, distant places.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢那种对偏远遥远之地的疯狂入侵。

sentences.en: That's his vibe, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是他的风格，对吧？

sentences.en: He loves all that.
sentences.zh: 他最喜欢那一套了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A wheeze.
sentences.zh: 简直是个馊主意。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he's very keen on the idea of landing in Norway.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常热衷于在挪威登陆的想法。

sentences.en: And he also wanted to attack Soviet oil fields in Baku, in Azerbaijan.
sentences.zh: 他还想袭击阿塞拜疆巴库的苏联油田。

sentences.en: I mean, that seems mad.
sentences.zh: 我的天，这听起来太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Anyway, after a lot of dithering about this, the French and the British finally agree they will intervene in Norway.
sentences.zh: 总之，在对此犹豫不决了一通之后，法英两国终于同意干预挪威。

sentences.en: They will mine the waters around Narvik.
sentences.zh: 他们要在纳尔维克周边的水域布雷。

sentences.en: That's the crucial port the Germans get their iron ore from.
sentences.zh: 那是德国人获取铁矿石的关键港口。

sentences.en: Now, they know that if they mine these waters, there will be a German reaction.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们知道如果在这里布雷，德国人一定会作出反应。

sentences.en: So they say we'll also have to send troops and occupy Norway's western port.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，我们还得派军队去占领挪威的西部港口。

sentences.en: So that's Narvik, Stavanger, Bergen, places like that.
sentences.zh: 也就是纳尔维克、斯塔万格、卑尔根之类的地方。

sentences.en: And how do the Norwegians feel about this?
sentences.zh: 那挪威人对此作何感想？

sentences.en: Gutted, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想应该是心碎欲绝吧。

sentences.en: Are they told or are they just going to turn up and occupy them?
sentences.zh: 他们是事先被告知了，还是对方直接打上门来占领？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: As we shall see, the Norwegians, when the war breaks out, they don't know who started it, the Allies or the Germans.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，战争爆发时，挪威人甚至不知道是谁挑起的，是盟军还是德国人。

sentences.en: So that tells its own story, really.
sentences.zh: 所以这本身就说明问题了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So at the beginning of April, Churchill, who was really responsible for all this and basically ought to carry the can when it goes horribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以在四月初，这一切的罪魁祸首丘吉尔，当事情搞得一团糟时，基本上理应由他来背锅。

sentences.en: I mean, it's so Gallipoli, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太像加里波利战役了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, he never learns, really, does he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他真是死性不改，对吧？

sentences.en: He decides he'll kick it off.
sentences.zh: 他决定由他来打响第一枪。

sentences.en: He sends four destroyers to lay these mines.
sentences.zh: 他派了四艘驱逐舰去布设这些水雷。

sentences.en: But I mean, I guess the reason that he doesn't end up carrying the can is because Chamberlain, on the 3rd of April,
sentences.zh: 但我想，他之所以最后没有背锅，是因为张伯伦在4月3日那天——

sentences.en: he addresses the Conservative National Union and he makes a kind of fateful boast, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他在保守党国民联盟发表了演讲，吹了个命运攸关的大牛，不是吗？

sentences.en: Whatever reason Hitler had for not making an immediate endeavour to overwhelm us, one thing is certain, he has missed the bus.
sentences.zh: 不管希特勒出于什么原因没有立即全力压倒我们，但有一点是肯定的，他错失良机了。

sentences.en: And that phrase, Hitler has missed the bus, will return to haunt Chamberlain.
sentences.zh: 而“希特勒错失良机”这句话，日后将化作挥之不去的阴影折磨着张伯伦。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 的确如此。

sentences.en: Because actually, while the Allies have been messing around and dithering with their mad ideas,
sentences.zh: 因为事实上，正当盟军还在为他们那些疯狂的想法瞎折腾、犹豫不决时，

sentences.en: Hitler has made up his own mind and he has already sent the German fleet to begin the operation against Norway.
sentences.zh: 希特勒已经下定决心，并且已经派出德国舰队开始执行针对挪威的行动了。

sentences.en: Now, the British, this speaks volumes about the quality of Britain's decision-making at this point, the British have intelligence to say the Germans are put to sea.
sentences.zh: 至于英国人嘛，这充分说明了当时英国决策的质量，英国人收到了情报，说德国舰队已经出海。

sentences.en: But they say, yeah, they're probably not going to Norway.
sentences.zh: 但他们却说，没事，他们大概不是去挪威的。

sentences.en: I imagine they're going to try and break through into the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 我猜他们是想强行突入大西洋。

sentences.en: So, you know, let's not overstress about that.
sentences.zh: 所以呢，大家用不着那么紧张。

sentences.en: Early on the 8th of April, the British start to lay their mines outside Narvik.
sentences.zh: 4月8日一大早，英国人开始在纳尔维克外海布雷。

sentences.en: But the Germans are approaching all the time.
sentences.zh: 但德国舰队一直在逼近。

sentences.en: My brother's brilliant on this.
sentences.zh: 我弟弟在这方面的研究太棒了。

sentences.en: And he writes, it was incredible that after so much allied vacillation over Norway,
sentences.zh: 他写道，真难以置信，在盟友对挪威犹豫不决了这么久之后，

sentences.en: both sides should have been beginning their offensives at the same moment and both be ignorant of the other's plans.
sentences.zh: 双方竟然在同一时刻开始发动进攻，并且对彼此的计划一无所知。

sentences.en: I mean, that is kind of mad, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直太疯狂了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's crazy.
sentences.zh: 太荒谬了。

sentences.en: So, midnight on the 8th, the Norwegians realise something is up.
sentences.zh: 所以在8日午夜，挪威人意识到情况不对劲了。

sentences.en: And the Norwegian side of the story is great, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实，从挪威人的角度来看，这段历史非常精彩。

sentences.en: And I shall be referring listeners to some excellent films on this made in Norway.
sentences.zh: 我稍后会向听众推荐几部在挪威拍摄的关于此事的优秀电影。

sentences.en: It's about 1.30 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 当时大约是凌晨一点半。

sentences.en: An aide comes in to wake the king, who is called Håkon VII.
sentences.zh: 一名副官进来叫醒国王，国王名叫哈康七世。

sentences.en: And he is a very sort of tall, gaunt man, if you Google him.
sentences.zh: 如果你去谷歌一下，会发现他是个身材高大、面容消瘦的人。

sentences.en: He's actually a Dane.
sentences.zh: 其实他是丹麦人。

sentences.en: So, they had to pick a new king when they broke away from Sweden at the beginning of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 所以在20世纪初脱离瑞典独立时，他们不得不挑选一位新国王。

sentences.en: And they'd picked this Danish bloke.
sentences.zh: 然后他们挑中了这个丹麦家伙。

sentences.en: He's got an absolutely first-class moustache.
sentences.zh: 他留着一把绝对一流的胡子。

sentences.en: He sent his son to Balliol College, Oxford, which I think reflects very well on him.
sentences.zh: 他把儿子送去了牛津大学贝利奥尔学院，我觉得这对他很有眼光。

sentences.en: Anyway, there he is in bed.
sentences.zh: 总之，他当时正躺在床上。

sentences.en: And his aide says, Majesty, we're at war.
sentences.zh: 他的副官说，陛下，我们开战了。

sentences.en: And the king says, with whom?
sentences.zh: 国王问，和谁？

sentences.en: You know, because they don't know whether it's going to be the Germans or the Allies.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，因为他们根本不知道来的是德国人还是盟军。

sentences.en: Exactly the same thing happens in Iceland, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 冰岛发生的情况完全一样，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The British do go and occupy Iceland.
sentences.zh: 英国人确实去占领了冰岛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And they say, who is it?
sentences.zh: 然后他们问，是谁啊？

sentences.en: And they say the British.
sentences.zh: 对方回答说是英国人。

sentences.en: And they go, phew.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就松了一口气。

sentences.en: Because better the British than the Germans, I guess.
sentences.zh: 因为我猜，比起德国人，还是英国人好一点。

sentences.en: It's nice that people think that way about us.
sentences.zh: 人们对我们有这种看法，挺让人欣慰的。

sentences.en: I'm sure everybody in the world thinks that way about when the British turn up, don't they?
sentences.zh: 我确信世界上每个人在英国人出现时都是这么想的，对吧？

sentences.en: That's the impression I get from the history books I read.
sentences.zh: 这是我从读过的历史书中得到的印象。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: So, there's a very comic side to the Norwegian resistance.
sentences.zh: 所以，挪威人的抵抗中有着非常滑稽的一面。

sentences.en: So, this is my favourite bit.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的一个片段。

sentences.en: Norway's commander-in-chief was an elderly general called General Larker.
sentences.zh: 挪威的最高指挥官是一位年迈的将军，名叫拉尔克将军。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't think Norwegians had ever really, not since Harald Hardrada really, had they extended themselves militarily.
sentences.zh: 对，我想挪威人从来没有——自从哈拉尔·哈德拉达以来，就再没有真正在军事上展露过身手。

sentences.en: So, General Larker is told, the Germans are coming up the Oslo Fjord.
sentences.zh: 所以，有人通知拉尔克将军：德国人正顺着奥斯陆峡湾开上来。

sentences.en: Ships are, you know, coming through the fog or whatever.
sentences.zh: 军舰正穿过浓雾开过来，诸如此类的。

sentences.en: And he says, right, call out the reserves.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，好吧，把预备役叫来。

sentences.en: Like, send out the letters.
sentences.zh: 就像是，发信件通知他们。

sentences.en: And someone said, what, the letters?
sentences.zh: 有人问，什么，发信件？

sentences.zh: 我们居然打算全靠邮政来搞定这一切。

sentences.zh: 对，你知道挪威的邮政是什么德行。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Anyway, staff officers remonstrated with him.
sentences.zh: 总之，参谋军官们纷纷向他进谏。

sentences.en: And he said, it's fine.
sentences.zh: 而他说，没关系。

sentences.en: There's no hurry.
sentences.zh: 不着急。

sentences.en: Don't overthink this.
sentences.zh: 别想太多。

sentences.zh: 只管给他们写信就行。

sentences.en: They'll turn up.
sentences.zh: 他们会到的。

sentences.en: And then he said, I need to go back to my farm.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，我得回我的农场一趟。

sentences.en: This is my favourite detail.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的细节。

sentences.en: To get my toilet dress.
sentences.zh: 去拿我的洗漱包。

sentences.en: He basically has to get his wash bag from his farm.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是得回农场去拿他的洗漱包。

sentences.en: It's outside Oslo.
sentences.zh: 那地方在奥斯陆郊外。

sentences.en: He goes out to his farm and collects his, like, change of clothes, underwear, you know, toothbrush, whatever.
sentences.zh: 他回到农场去收拾他的换洗衣服、内衣、牙刷什么的。

sentences.en: And then he calls a taxi.
sentences.zh: 然后他叫了一辆出租车。

sentences.en: But because the invasion has begun, the taxi is very, very severely delayed.
sentences.zh: 但由于入侵已经开始，出租车非常、非常严重地延误了。

sentences.en: It takes ages for this taxi to arrive.
sentences.zh: 这辆出租车花了极长的时间才到。

sentences.en: The taxi picks him up and takes him back to Oslo to a Norwegian army headquarters.
sentences.zh: 出租车接上他，把他带回奥斯陆的一个挪威陆军指挥部。

sentences.en: By the time he gets there with his wash bag, the general staff have evacuated and they haven't left any information to tell him where they've gone.
sentences.zh: 等他带着洗漱包赶到那里时，总参谋部已经撤离了，而且没有留下任何信息告诉他他们去了哪里。

sentences.en: This isn't the spirit of Harold Hardrada, is it?
sentences.zh: 这可不是哈拉尔德·哈德拉达的精神，对吧？

sentences.en: So, he then, he works out where they've gone.
sentences.zh: 所以，然后他，他算出了他们去了哪里。

sentences.en: He gets a tram, a suburban tram, carrying his stuff as far as he can to the end of the line.
sentences.zh: 他坐了一辆电车，一辆郊区电车，带着他的行李，能坐多远就坐多远，直到终点站。

sentences.en: And then he walked to the Norwegian Map Institute to see if they had a car that he could borrow to take him to meet his men.
sentences.zh: 然后他步行去挪威地图研究所，看看他们有没有车可以借给他，带他去见他的部下。

sentences.en: They don't have a car.
sentences.zh: 他们没有车。

sentences.en: So, then he had to walk all the way back to the railway station to get a train.
sentences.zh: 所以，他不得不一路走回火车站去坐火车。

sentences.en: And it's hours and hours until he finally rejoins his stuff.
sentences.zh: 他花了数小时的时间，才终于重新与他的行李汇合。

sentences.en: So, blitzkrieg, it is not.
sentences.zh: 所以，闪击战根本谈不上。

sentences.en: Well, do you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: That sounds like I'm dissing the Norwegians.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是在贬低挪威人。

sentences.en: I'm not because they put up some pretty stout resistance.
sentences.zh: 我可没有，因为他们进行了相当顽强的抵抗。

sentences.en: The Germans have come up the Oslofjord in this cruiser, the Blücher, with thousands of troops.
sentences.zh: 德国人乘这艘名为布吕歇尔号的巡洋舰带着数千名部队顺奥斯陆峡湾而上。

sentences.en: There's a whole film about this called Blücher, a Norwegian film that came out in September.
sentences.zh: 有一部关于这件事的完整电影叫《布吕歇尔》，是一部九月份上映的挪威电影。

sentences.en: You can see clips from it on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 你可以在优酷或YouTube上看到它的片段。

sentences.en: The Norwegians have this fortress called the Oskarsbjörg, and it has two 19th century antique cannons.
sentences.zh: 挪威人有一个叫奥斯卡斯堡的要塞，里面有两门19世纪的古董大农炮。

sentences.en: And basically, this Blücher comes closer and closer.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这艘布吕歇尔号越来越近。

sentences.en: These guys wait at this fortress until it's really close.
sentences.zh: 这些人在要塞里等待，直到它非常靠近。

sentences.en: Then they fire with these antique cannons.
sentences.zh: 然后他们用这些古董大炮开火。

sentences.en: They hit the Blücher's fuel store.
sentences.zh: 他们击中了布吕歇尔号的油库。

sentences.en: The Blücher explodes, bursts into flames, and explodes, and 800 of the Germans were drowned.
sentences.zh: 布吕歇尔号爆炸了，燃起熊熊大火，再次爆炸，800名德国人淹死了。

sentences.en: So, it was a big win, that, for the Norwegians.
sentences.zh: 所以，对挪威人来说，这是一场大胜。

sentences.en: And because of scenes like this, this gave the king, King Holken and his ministers, time to get out of Oslo.
sentences.zh: 正是因为这样的场景，才为主持大局的国王霍肯国王和他的大臣们争取到了离开奥斯陆的时间。

sentences.en: They managed to smuggle out the gold reserves as well, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们还成功地把黄金储备偷运出去了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Kind of pretty much under the noses of the Germans.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以说是从德国人的眼皮底下溜走的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great story.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个伟大的故事。

sentences.en: I mean, as we'll see, it makes a great film.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我们所见，它拍成了一部好电影。

sentences.en: Because they head to this village called Elverum, which is about 40 miles north of Oslo.
sentences.zh: 因为他们前往一个叫做埃尔弗鲁姆的村庄，那里在奥斯陆以北约40英里处。

sentences.en: And they're being pursued the whole time by German paratroopers, who've been basically told, get the Norwegian government and get the king.
sentences.zh: 他们一路上都在被德国伞兵追捕，这些伞兵的任务基本上就是抓住挪威政府和国王。

sentences.en: We'll need them.
sentences.zh: 我们会需要他们的。

sentences.en: The local rifle club, the Elverum Rifle Club, put up a roadblock and basically drove back these German paratroopers.
sentences.zh: 当地的步枪俱乐部，埃尔弗鲁姆步枪俱乐部，设置了路障，基本上把这些德国伞兵击退了。

sentences.en: I mean, that's incredible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: These blokes were like hunting rifles or whatever.
sentences.zh: 这些家伙拿着的就像是猎枪之类的东西。

sentences.en: These ordinary Norwegians managed to drive them back.
sentences.zh: 这些普通的挪威人竟然成功击退了他们。

sentences.en: And that gave the king and his entourage time to get away.
sentences.zh: 这为主办方和国王及随行人员争取了逃跑的时间。

sentences.en: And they had a meeting.
sentences.zh: 他们开了一个会。

sentences.en: And basically, the king is told, the Germans want Quisling to run a puppet government, and you have to approve it.
sentences.zh: 基本上，国王被告知，德国人想要吉斯林来管理一个傀儡政府，你必须批准。

sentences.en: And the king says, it's a very sort of stirring scene.
sentences.zh: 国王说，这是一个非常感人的场景。

sentences.en: He says to his ministers, look, there's no way I'm going to accept this.
sentences.zh: 他对大臣们说，听着，我绝不可能接受这个。

sentences.en: No way whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 绝无可能。

sentences.en: He says, if you want to accept it, fine.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果你们想接受，那随便。

sentences.en: But I will abdicate.
sentences.zh: 但我会退位。

sentences.en: I will never, ever preside over a Quisling government.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会、绝不会主持一个吉斯林政府。

sentences.en: And then he bursts into tears.
sentences.zh: 然后他失声痛哭。

sentences.en: And it's a very stirring scene.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常感人的场面。

sentences.en: There's a Norwegian film of this called The King's Choice.
sentences.zh: 有一部关于这事的挪威电影叫《国王的选择》。

sentences.en: I fell down a massive rabbit hole and ended up watching huge chunks of this film.
sentences.zh: 我掉进了一个巨大的深坑，最后看了这部电影的大量片段。

sentences.en: It's really moving, actually.
sentences.zh: 说实话，真的很感人。

sentences.en: It's a really moving story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常感人的故事。

sentences.en: Now, meanwhile, further south, the Germans have also invaded Denmark, which is the country that King Hagen had been born into, because he's from the Danish royal family originally.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在更南边，德国人还入侵了丹麦，这也是哈根国王出生的国家，因为他原本来自丹麦王室。

sentences.en: And there, the story is a bit different.
sentences.zh: 在那里，情况就有点不同了。

sentences.en: And I mean that as no disrespect to the Danes.
sentences.zh: 我这么说对丹麦人绝无不敬。

sentences.en: But the geography is just not in the Danes' favour.
sentences.zh: 但地理条件对丹麦人实在太不利了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, also, they've got a land border with Germany.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们与德国接壤。

sentences.en: So the panzers, presumably, can just roll through Schleswig-Holstein.
sentences.zh: 所以装甲部队大概可以长驱直入石勒苏益格-荷尔斯泰因。

sentences.en: Which is exactly what they do.
sentences.zh: 这正是他们所做的。

sentences.en: So they kick off at 4.15 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在清晨4点15分开始行动。

sentences.en: The panzers roll over, naval landings, paratroopers, and the Danes are completely nuttily helpless.
sentences.zh: 装甲部队碾压过来，海军登陆，伞兵突袭，丹麦人完全无能为力。

sentences.en: There's a bit of fighting around the royal palace in Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 哥本哈根王宫周围发生了一些战斗。

sentences.en: But the king of Denmark, Christian X, who is actually the Norwegian king's older brother, he can see that this is totally pointless.
sentences.zh: 但丹麦国王克里斯蒂安十世，他实际上是挪威国王的哥哥，他看出这一切毫无意义。

sentences.en: There's no geographical barriers.
sentences.zh: 没有任何地理屏障。

sentences.en: The Germans are just sort of rolling into Denmark.
sentences.zh: 德国人正在涌入丹麦。

sentences.en: And by breakfast, he is ordered a ceasefire.
sentences.zh: 到早餐时，他已经下令停火。

sentences.en: And they signed the capitulation at 10 o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 他们在早上10点签署了投降书。

sentences.en: That was the shortest campaign of the entire war.
sentences.zh: 那是整个战争中最短的战役。

sentences.en: So that's five and three-quarters hours.
sentences.zh: 也就是五个半小时加十五分钟。

sentences.en: Yeah, from start to finish.
sentences.zh: 是的，从头到尾。

sentences.en: Like, it's perfectly plausible that if you had a lion that day,
sentences.zh: 就像是，如果你那天养了一只狮子，完全有可能

sentences.en: you could wake up and not know that an invasion had happened and was finished.
sentences.zh: 你醒来时根本不知道发生过入侵并且已经结束了。

sentences.en: So my brother goes so far as to say, surely the fastest conquest of a country in history.
sentences.zh: 所以我的兄弟甚至说，这绝对是历史上对一个国家最快的征服。

sentences.en: Yeah, quite possibly.
sentences.zh: 是的，很有可能。

sentences.en: And actually, I definitely don't want to disrespect the king of Denmark, because King Christian, he didn't go into exile, as many monarchs did,
sentences.zh: 实际上，我绝对不想对丹麦国王不敬，因为克里斯蒂安国王并没有像许多君主那样流亡，

sentences.en: because his son's wife, Crown Princess Ingrid, who was, I think, Swedish, she was nine months pregnant and she couldn't travel.
sentences.zh: 因为他儿子的妻子、王储妃英格丽德，我想她是瑞典人，当时怀孕九个月了，无法旅行。

sentences.en: So he has to stay in Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 所以他不得不留在哥本哈根。

sentences.en: But he behaves tremendously well, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他表现得非常出色，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Very moving and powerful symbol of resistance.
sentences.zh: 抵抗运动非常感人和强大的象征。

sentences.en: Very moving.
sentences.zh: 非常感人。

sentences.en: He rides every day through Copenhagen on his horse.
sentences.zh: 他每天骑着马穿过哥本哈根。

sentences.en: And the people gather and they cheer him and stuff.
sentences.zh: 人们聚集在一起为他欢呼之类的事。

sentences.en: Everyone knows he is not keen on the Nazis and all of this.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道他不喜欢纳粹以及这一切。

sentences.en: And most famously, he said to the Germans, if you make the Danish Jews wear yellow stars, then I will wear one too.
sentences.zh: 最著名的是，他对德国人说，如果你们让丹麦犹太人戴黄星，那我也戴一个。

sentences.en: And basically, all my people will wear them.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我所有的人民都会戴上它们。

sentences.en: I think it reflects tremendously well on him.
sentences.zh: 我认为这充分体现了他的伟大。

sentences.en: You can see, again, you can see footage online of him riding through Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 你同样可以在网上看到他骑马穿过哥本哈根的镜头。

sentences.en: Good for him.
sentences.zh: 做得好。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: But the Norwegians can hold out much longer because of the mountains and stuff.
sentences.zh: 但挪威人因为山脉等原因能够坚持更长时间。

sentences.en: So by contrast, that campaign lasted for two months, longer than any other German invasion campaign, except for the invasion of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，那场战役持续了两个月，比除了入侵苏联之外的任何其他德国入侵战役都要长。

sentences.en: So fair play to the Norwegians.
sentences.zh: 所以给挪威人点赞。

sentences.en: And they were not a martial people, but about 40,000 of them immediately volunteered.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是一个尚武的民族，但大约有四万人立即志愿参军。

sentences.en: They fought very bravely.
sentences.zh: 他们战斗得非常勇敢。

sentences.en: They didn't have decent equipment, but they really acquitted themselves well.
sentences.zh: 他们没有像样的装备，但他们的表现确实很出色。

sentences.en: Now, we are a patriotic podcast, but unfortunately, this is not something that can be said of the British or our gallant allies, the French.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们是一个爱国播客，但不幸的是，英国人或我们英勇的盟友法国人却不能这么说。

sentences.en: Did they let themselves down?
sentences.zh: 他们让自己失望了吗？

sentences.en: We absolutely disgraced ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对是让自己蒙羞了。

sentences.zh: 用马克斯·黑斯廷斯在他关于第二次世界大战的书中的话说，我们的战役的特点是彻底的道义卑劣和军事无能。

sentences.en: So that's a shame.
sentences.zh: 这真是遗憾。

sentences.en: Dear.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So basically, part of this is because a lot of the best troops are stationed in France.
sentences.zh: 基本上，部分原因是因为许多最好的军队都驻扎在法国。

sentences.en: So the British government sent some territorial reserve battalions, and they were absolutely useless.
sentences.zh: 所以英国政府派了一些领土预备营，他们完全是废物。

sentences.en: They didn't have maps, a lot of them.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人没有地图。

sentences.en: They didn't have radios.
sentences.zh: 他们没有无线电设备。

sentences.en: They didn't have heavy weapons.
sentences.zh: 他们没有重武器。

sentences.en: They had the wrong shoes, ironically.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，他们穿错了鞋子。

sentences.en: Oh, did they?
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗？

sentences.en: They did.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Oh, well, we like that.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，我们喜欢这样。

sentences.en: They get into fights with local fishermen.
sentences.zh: 他们与当地渔民打架。

sentences.en: My favorite moment, Admiral Lord Cork, who was a very short man, wants to inspire his men to get off their ships and advance on Narvik.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的时刻，身材非常矮小的科克勋爵海军上将，想要激励他的部下离开他们的船只向纳尔维克推进。

sentences.en: And they're very reluctant to do so.
sentences.zh: 他们非常不情愿这样做。

sentences.en: And he says, I'll lead you ashore.
sentences.zh: 他说，我带你们上岸。

sentences.en: And he gets off the ship.
sentences.zh: 然后他下了船。

sentences.en: And because he's a very short man, he falls into a snowdrift and has to be dug out by the rest of the men.
sentences.zh: 因为他个子非常矮，所以掉进了雪堆里，必须由其他人把他挖出来。

sentences.en: So not the most glorious moment in British military history.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是英国军事史上最光彩的时刻。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: So we did land in central Norway.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实在中挪威登陆了。

sentences.en: We did capture Narvik and then recapture it.
sentences.zh: 我们确实占领了纳尔维克然后又重新占领了它。

sentences.en: But basically, Churchill is constantly coming up with schemes of various kinds, which end up being ditched.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，丘吉尔不断提出各种计划，结果却都被放弃了。

sentences.en: To quote Max Hastings again,
sentences.zh: 引用马克斯·黑斯廷斯的话，

sentences.en: Churchill shouted loudest, but his extravagant schemes were frustrated by the lack of means to fulfill them.
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔叫嚣得最厉害，但他那些浮夸的计划因缺乏实现它们的手段而受挫。

sentences.en: Do you know what's even worse about that?
sentences.zh: 你知道关于这更糟的是什么吗？

sentences.en: In his office in the Admiralty, opposite his desk, who do you think Churchill has a portrait of?
sentences.zh: 在他在海军部的办公室里，就在他办公桌对面，你认为丘吉尔挂着谁的肖像？

sentences.en: Surely Admiral Lord Nelson.
sentences.zh: 当然是纳尔逊勋爵海军上将。

sentences.en: It is Admiral Lord Nelson, whose record in Scandinavian conflict was a whole lot better.
sentences.zh: 正是纳尔逊勋爵海军上将，他在斯堪的纳维亚冲突中的战绩要好得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But also, Nelson was rubbish on land, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，纳尔逊在陆地上也是个废柴。

sentences.zh: 所以在挪威的登陆正是纳尔逊会搞得一团糟的那种事情。

sentences.en: Do you not think?
sentences.zh: 你不这么认为吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, but not as big a hash as Churchill did.
sentences.zh: 是的，但没有丘吉尔搞得那么糟。

sentences.en: As Churchill made of Norway.
sentences.zh: 就像丘吉尔把挪威搞砸了一样。

sentences.en: And the worst thing is, when the British and French decide to pull the plug, and they're going to have to evacuate, they didn't have the decency to tell the Norwegians.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的是，当英法决定拔掉电源并不得不撤离时，他们却没有风度去告诉挪威人。

sentences.en: So they were dishonest with them until the final moment.
sentences.zh: 所以直到最后一刻他们还在对他们不诚实。

sentences.en: But that is only possible if it's already received a knockout blow.
sentences.zh: 但这只有在英国已经遭受致命打击的情况下才有可能。

sentences.en: So it there is England.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果存在英国的话。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the knockout blow is to beat France, what Goebbels calls an act of historical justice against the French that will leave Britain friendless on the continent.
sentences.zh: 而致命一击就是击败法国，戈培尔称这是对法国人的一次历史公正的审判，这将使英国在欧洲大陆上孤立无援。

sentences.en: So how are they going to do it?
sentences.zh: 那么他们将如何做到这一点呢？

sentences.en: So if you look at the two sets of forces on paper, they're actually pretty well matched.
sentences.zh: 如果你从纸面上看这两支军队，它们其实势均力敌。

sentences.en: The French have more tanks, they have 3,000 tanks, the Germans 2,000.
sentences.zh: 法国人拥有更多坦克，他们有3000辆坦克，德国人有2000辆。

sentences.en: The French have much more artillery.
sentences.zh: 法国人拥有多得多的火炮。

sentences.en: The Germans have about 90 divisions, a division very roughly, about 15,000 men.
sentences.zh: 德国人大约有90个师，一个师大致相当于1.5万人。

sentences.en: The French have got the same and the British have got another 10 divisions, always much smaller on land than the British.
sentences.zh: 法国人也有同样多的兵力，英国人则有另外10个师，在陆地上英国人总是规模要小得多。

sentences.en: But the Germans have got a couple of advantages.
sentences.zh: 但德国人有几个优势。

sentences.en: They've got slightly more fighters and bombers than the Allies do in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 他们在西线拥有的战斗机和轰炸机比盟军略多一些。

sentences.en: And they have learned in Poland how they can use them.
sentences.zh: 他们在波兰学会了如何使用这些飞机。

sentences.en: They can use them in cooperation with their ground troops to full effect, which the British and French have not learned how to do.
sentences.zh: 他们能够将飞机与地面部队配合使用，发挥出全部威力，而英国人和法国人还没有学会这一点。

sentences.en: That is true, that they do have some battle-hardened troops.
sentences.zh: 的确，他们确实拥有一些身经百战的部队。

sentences.en: However, because everyone knows what is going to come, and because Nazi propaganda has been harping on the ruthless, invincible, mechanized nature of the German war machine.
sentences.zh: 然而，由于每个人都知道即将发生什么，而且纳粹宣传一直在喋喋不休地强调德国战争机器冷酷无情、不可战胜、机械化的本质。

sentences.en: And so the success of the Nazi troops in the invasion of France will kind of retrospectively burnish that propaganda.
sentences.zh: 因此，纳粹军队在入侵法国时的成功将在某种程度上事后为这种宣传增光添彩。

sentences.en: I said in my brother's book, The War in the West, he talks about this Potemkin quality of Nazi militarism.
sentences.zh: 正如我在我兄弟的书《西线战争》中所说，他谈到了纳粹军国主义这种波将金式的虚假表象。

sentences.en: So actually, overall, the Allies do have more planes between them than the Luftwaffe, overall.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，总体而言，盟军拥有的飞机数量确实比德国空军多。

sentences.en: And actually, the German troops, only half of all of them, have had more than a few weeks training, more than a quarter of over 40.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，德国士兵中只有一半接受过几周以上的训练，超过四分之一的人年过40。

sentences.en: The artillery, the German artillery, is designed to be drawn by horses.
sentences.zh: 火炮，德国的火炮，设计上是由马匹牵引的。

sentences.en: And of the 135 divisions that have been earmarked for the invasion of France, of those, only 10 are panzer, and only six are fully mechanized.
sentences.zh: 在为入侵法国而指定预留的135个师中，只有10个是装甲师，只有6个是完全机械化部队。

sentences.en: So the idea that the whole German army is kind of the cutting edge of modern fighting forces simply isn't true.
sentences.zh: 因此，整个德国军队可以说是现代战斗部队尖端力量这种说法根本不是真的。

sentences.en: I really hadn't properly appreciated that.
sentences.zh: 我以前确实没有好好体会这一点。

sentences.en: And I think it does kind of put the looming calamity for French and British arms into an even more sharper perspective, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实让英法军队即将来临的灾难显得更加严峻。

sentences.en: They are not beaten by an overwhelmingly mechanized force.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是被一支压倒性的机械化部队击败的。

sentences.en: No, no, no, they're not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，根本不是。

sentences.en: What I would say is the Germans do still win, though.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，德国人最终还是赢了。

sentences.en: So, I mean, we shouldn't go to the other extreme and suggest that they're completely useless.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我们不应该走向另一个极端，认为他们完全一无是处。

sentences.en: No, they're not.
sentences.zh: 不，他们并非如此。

sentences.en: I mean, as we'll see, they have good tactics.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我们将看到的，他们拥有良好的战术。

sentences.en: But I think it also reflects on the grotesque incompetence of the Allies in the test that is to come.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这也反映出盟军即将面临的考验中表现出的极度无能。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, we've talked about how incompetent the Allies were in Norway.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，我们已经讨论过盟军在挪威的表现是多么无能。

sentences.en: Their planning and their intelligence in the Western campaign, in this campaign, are unbelievably useless.
sentences.zh: 他们在西线战役中的规划和情报简直无能到令人难以置信。

sentences.en: They seem to have no sense of how quickly armored divisions can move.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎完全没有意识到装甲师的移动速度有多快。

sentences.en: The French are always fighting the last war.
sentences.zh: 法国人总是在打上一场战争。

sentences.en: It's mad that in the First World War they were fighting the Franco-Prussian War and the Napoleonic Wars.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的是，在第一次世界大战中，他们还在打普法战争和拿破仑战争。

sentences.en: And now they think they're fighting the First World War.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们以为自己在打第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: So they're all geared up for kind of trenches and all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们全神贯注于战壕之类的事情。

sentences.en: And it's as though tanks have not yet been invented.
sentences.zh: 这就好像坦克根本还没被发明出来一样。

sentences.en: And actually, General Bégon, who takes command of the French armies on the 25th of May, by which point it's obvious that France is completely defeated,
sentences.zh: 事实上，于5月25日接管法国军队指挥权的韦冈将军，当时法国彻底战败已成定局

sentences.en: he said, we've gone to war with the 1918 army against the German army of 1939, which in terms of equipment isn't true, but in terms of attitude is clearly the case.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们是用1918年的军队去对抗1939年的德国军队，从装备上讲这不是真的，但从态度上讲显然就是这么回事。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So let's get into a little bit of military strategy, because an absolutely key French failure and British failure, they completely fail to predict the Germans' line of attack.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们进入一点军事战略，因为法国和英国犯下的一个绝对关键的错误是，他们完全未能预测到德国人的进攻路线。

sentences.en: So as we saw last time, Hitler wanted to attack straight away in the autumn of 1939, but because there was a lot of dithering and mainly because of the weather, that was postponed.
sentences.zh: 正如我们上次所看到的，希特勒希望在1939年秋天直接发动进攻，但由于许多犹豫不决以及主要是天气原因，进攻被推迟了。

sentences.en: And that has given the Germans time to refine their plans.
sentences.zh: 这给了德国人时间来完善他们的计划。

sentences.en: So people who listen to our First World War series will have heard a lot about things like the Schlieffen Plan and all the difficulties that the Germans faced in 1914.
sentences.zh: 因此，听过我们第一次世界大战系列的听众会听到很多关于施里芬计划以及德国人在1914年面临的所有困难。

sentences.en: Their plan in 1939-1940 was initially very similar.
sentences.zh: 他们1939年至1940年的计划最初非常相似。

sentences.en: They would go through Belgium and Holland because they want to get around the Maginot Line, which are these forts the French had built to defend Alsace and Lorraine further south.
sentences.zh: 他们将穿过比利时和荷兰，因为他们想绕过马奇诺防线，这是法国人为保卫更南边的阿尔萨斯和洛林而修建的要塞。

sentences.en: The original German plan was to go through Belgium and Holland.
sentences.zh: 最初的德国计划是通过比利时和荷兰。

sentences.en: Very First World War, we push the French back to the Somme, and then we kind of grind them down there.
sentences.zh: 非常具有一战风格，我们将法国人逼退到索姆河，然后在那里进行消耗战。

sentences.en: And when that plan was presented to Hitler, he didn't like it.
sentences.zh: 当这个计划呈交给希特勒时，他并不喜欢。

sentences.en: He said, I just think this feels very 1914.
sentences.zh: 他说，我只是觉得这太有1914年的感觉了。

sentences.en: It's very unoriginal.
sentences.zh: 毫无新意。

sentences.en: Yeah, I want something.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想要点别的。

sentences.en: I want a decisive, exciting, original, you know, stroke, speed and surprise.
sentences.zh: 我想要果断、刺激、原创的举措，速度和奇袭。

sentences.en: That's what I'm all about.
sentences.zh: 这正是我所追求的。

sentences.en: Now, meanwhile, two other generals, Eric von Manstein and a panzer commander,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，另外两位将军埃里希·冯·曼施坦因和一位装甲部队指挥官

sentences.en: Heinz Guderian, had been working on a rival plan.
sentences.zh: 海因茨·古德里安一直在制定一项针锋相对的计划。

sentences.en: This plan, they said, look, why don't we just pretend effectively to go through Belgium and Holland, the low countries?
sentences.zh: 他们说，听着，我们为什么不实际上假装通过比利时和荷兰这些低地国家呢？

sentences.en: Why don't we concentrate our tanks a little bit further south and go through the Ardenne forest?
sentences.zh: 为什么不把我们的坦克集中在更南一点的地方，穿过阿登森林呢？

sentences.en: Because it's the forest, everybody assumes it's kind of off limits and the French will leave it only lightly defended.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一片森林，每个人都认为这是禁区，法国人只会留驻少量防御兵力。

sentences.en: And the high command of the army, the Wehrmacht, thought this plan was deranged.
sentences.zh: 而德军最高统帅部认为这个计划简直疯了。

sentences.en: And they basically sent Manstein to East Prussia to shut him up, to get rid of him.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上把曼施坦因打发到东普鲁士去让他闭嘴，好把他支开。

sentences.en: But one person who doesn't is Guderian.
sentences.zh: 但有一个人没有这样做，那就是古德里安。

sentences.en: He, two years before, had written the most German army titled book of all time.
sentences.zh: 两年前，他写了一本最具德军风格的书。

sentences.en: Because its title was Akhtung Panzer, exclamation mark.
sentences.zh: 因为它的书名叫《注意，坦克！》，后面带个感叹号。

sentences.en: That's sort of a British comic from the 1970s, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那听起来像是20世纪70年代的英国漫画，对吧？

sentences.en: It's such a great title.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝佳的书名。

sentences.en: And he's Hitler's kind of man.
sentences.zh: 而且他正是希特勒想要的那种人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because he's all about speed.
sentences.zh: 因为他崇尚速度。

sentences.en: He's about the idea that you separate the panzers off from the much more cumbersome, slower moving infantry divisions and the artillery with their horses and things.
sentences.zh: 他的理念是将装甲部队从那些笨重、行动迟缓的步兵师以及带着马匹等装备的炮兵中分离出来。

sentences.en: And you just go for broke.
sentences.zh: 然后孤注一掷。

sentences.en: Speed.
sentences.zh: 速度。

sentences.en: So here's now a mad thing that happens, right?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了一件疯狂的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: The high command wants to go with their original plan, despite Hitler's misgivings.
sentences.zh: 最高统帅部尽管对希特勒的疑虑有所保留，但仍想执行他们最初的计划。

sentences.en: And then on the 10th of January, a Luftwaffe plane got lost in fog.
sentences.zh: 然后就在1月10日，一架德国空军飞机在雾中迷失了方向。

sentences.en: It accidentally flies into Belgium and it crashes in a field in Belgium.
sentences.zh: 它不小心飞入比利时，并在比利时的一个田野里坠毁。

sentences.en: And the passenger on the plane is called Major Reinberger.
sentences.zh: 机上的乘客名叫赖恩贝格尔少校。

sentences.en: And he is carrying the plan.
sentences.zh: 他随身携带作战计划。

sentences.en: And after the crash, the pilot and this bloke, Major Reinberger, were picked up by Belgian border guards who took them to a sort of hut.
sentences.zh: 坠机后，飞行员和这个叫赖恩贝格尔少校的家伙被比利时边防军截获，他们被带到一个类似棚屋的地方。

sentences.en: Don't forget, Belgium is neutral at this stage.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，比利时在这个阶段是中立国。

sentences.en: Major Reinberger tried to destroy their plans by stuffing them into a stove when the
sentences.zh: 趁比利时边防军不注意，赖恩贝格尔少校试图将作战计划塞进火炉里来销毁它们

sentences.en: Belgian border guards backs were turned.
sentences.zh: 比利时边防军转过身去。

sentences.en: I think he madly burnt his hands in the process trying to get the lid off the stove.
sentences.zh: 我想他在试图打开炉盖的过程中疯狂地把双手都烧伤了。

sentences.en: Anyway, the border guards managed to get the plans back out of the stove.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，边防军还是设法把计划从火炉里抢救了出来。

sentences.en: Major Reinberger at this point burst into tears and tried to shoot himself.
sentences.zh: 赖恩贝格尔少校此时失声痛哭，并试图开枪自杀。

sentences.en: Anyway, the upshot was the Allies say, oh, brilliant, we've got the German plans.
sentences.zh: 总之，结果就是盟军说，太棒了，我们得到了德国人的计划。

sentences.en: So we know for sure they're going to come through Belgium and Holland, just as we thought.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确切地知道他们会经由比利时和荷兰进攻，正如我们所料。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: We're laughing.
sentences.zh: 我们稳操胜券了。

sentences.en: So actually, it's like all those Allied plans to deceive the Germans about where D-Day landing is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这就像盟军为了迷惑德国人关于诺曼底登陆地点而做的所有那些欺骗计划一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Only they haven't actually fabricated it in this case.
sentences.zh: 只不过这次他们并没有凭空捏造。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: Now, in the meantime, the problem for the Allies, the Germans have changed their entire plan.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，对盟军来说麻烦的是，德国人已经改变了整个计划。

sentences.en: Hitler never liked that blueprint anyway.
sentences.zh: 希特勒反正一直不喜欢那个最初的蓝图。

sentences.en: He liked the idea of a surprise attack through the Ardennes as well.
sentences.zh: 他也喜欢通过阿登森林进行奇袭的想法。

sentences.en: And on the 17th of February, so a month after this crash, his adjutant invited Manstein to the Reich Chancellery.
sentences.zh: 2月17日，也就是这次坠机事件一个月后，他的副官邀请曼施坦因前往帝国总理府。

sentences.en: It basically said to him, come on, come and tell the Fuhrer about this mad idea of yours.
sentences.zh: 基本上是对他说，来吧，来向元首讲讲你这个疯狂的想法。

sentences.en: He'll love it.
sentences.zh: 他一定会喜欢的。

sentences.en: And Hitler doesn't like Manstein.
sentences.zh: 而且希特勒并不喜欢曼施坦因。

sentences.en: Now, Manstein's a very kind of cold, arrogant, Prussian aristocrat, the kind of person he's always distrustful of.
sentences.zh: 曼施坦因是一个非常冷漠、傲慢的普鲁士贵族，正是那种他一向不信任的人。

sentences.en: But he listens to the plan.
sentences.zh: 但他还是听取了这个计划。

sentences.en: He says, I've been gagging to hear a plan like this.
sentences.zh: 他说，我一直渴望听到这样的计划。

sentences.en: Through the Ardennes, surprise attack, reckless.
sentences.zh: 穿过阿登森林，奇袭，孤注一掷。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: I love the sound of it.
sentences.zh: 听起来妙极了。

sentences.en: Let's go for it.
sentences.zh: 就这么干吧。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So, this becomes the blueprint for Fall Gelb, Case Yellow, the German operation in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 于是，这成为了“黄色方案”（Fall Gelb）的蓝图，即德国在西线的军事行动。

sentences.en: Basically, there are two army groups.
sentences.zh: 基本上，有两个集团军群。

sentences.en: Army Group B is under Fedor von Bock.
sentences.zh: B集团军群由费多尔·冯·博克指挥。

sentences.en: How large is the other two army groups?
sentences.zh: 另外两个集团军群规模有多大？

sentences.en: So, Army Group B is 29 divisions, Tom.
sentences.zh: B集团军群有29个师，汤姆。

sentences.en: So, how many men is that?
sentences.zh: 那么那是多少人呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's 15,000 men.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是1.5万人。

sentences.en: You can do the math yourself.
sentences.zh: 你可以自己算算数。

sentences.en: Could you?
sentences.zh: 你会算吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, but I just don't want to.
sentences.zh: 会，但我就是不想算。

sentences.en: I'd like to give you a bit of a workout.
sentences.zh: 我想让你稍微锻炼一下脑子。

sentences.en: So, anyway, they've got 29 divisions, 15,000 men each.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们有29个师，每个师1.5万人。

sentences.en: Listeners can do the math.
sentences.zh: 听众们可以自己算算。

sentences.en: They will go through Belgium and Holland.
sentences.zh: 他们将穿过比利时和荷兰。

sentences.en: But this is a massive distraction exercise because the real action is going to come further south with Goethe von Rundstedt's Army Group A.
sentences.zh: 但这只是一次大规模的佯攻牵制，因为真正的重头戏将在南面由格特·冯·伦德施泰特的A集团军群上演。

sentences.en: And Army Group A has 44 divisions with loads of panzers and mechanized infantry.
sentences.zh: A集团军群拥有44个师，配有大量的装甲部队和机械化步兵。

sentences.en: And they are going to sneak through the woods of the Ardennes.
sentences.zh: 他们将悄悄穿过阿登森林。

sentences.en: And then this is the plan.
sentences.zh: 这就是计划。

sentences.en: When they're across, they'll get to the River Meuse and they'll cross the Meuse.
sentences.zh: 当他们穿过去后，他们将抵达默兹河并渡过默兹河。

sentences.en: But at that point, they won't carry on towards Paris, as the Allies will expect.
sentences.zh: 但到那个时候，他们不会像盟军所预料的那样继续向巴黎推进。

sentences.en: They will turn sharply to their right, in other words, turning north,
sentences.zh: 他们会急转右，换句话说，转向北方

sentences.en: and they will head up towards the coast of the English Channel in a kind of what's called a sickle-cut maneuver.
sentences.zh: 他们将以一种被称为“镰刀收割”的机动战术向英吉利海峡海岸挺进。

sentences.en: And what that means is that all the Allied French and British forces in Belgium will be trapped between the two German armies.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在比利时的所有盟军法军和英军将被夹在两支德国军队之间。

sentences.en: And they'll be pinned against the sea.
sentences.zh: 他们将被逼得背水一战。

sentences.en: And so this is the Battle of Cannae.
sentences.zh: 这就是坎尼会战。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, the great victory that Hannibal won over the Romans, and which have haunted, haunted the German military planning.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是汉尼拔对罗马人取得的伟大胜利，这一直挥之不去地萦绕在德国军事规划者的脑海中。

sentences.en: And so in a sense, although this seems tactically radical, strategically, it is what the Germans, you know, it's what they always come up with.
sentences.zh: 因此从某种意义上说，尽管这在战术上看起来很激进，但在战略上，这正是德国人一贯会想出来的招数。

sentences.en: And so that being so, you would think the French would have realized it.
sentences.zh: 既然如此，你本以为法国人会意识到这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just so mind-blowingly incompetent that they haven't sussed this out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们竟然没有察觉到这一点，简直是惊人的无能。

sentences.en: I'll make two observations.
sentences.zh: 我讲两点看法。

sentences.en: Number one is, I don't think there's ever been a battle, and the rest is history that you haven't likened to the Battle of Cannae.
sentences.zh: 第一点是，我觉得几乎没有哪场战役——剩下的历史大家也都知道——是你不会拿来与坎尼会战作类比的。

sentences.en: So that's the first point.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是第一点。

sentences.en: Listen, it's not me who's doing it.
sentences.zh: 听着，这不是我在这么做。

sentences.en: It's the German high command.
sentences.zh: 这是德国最高指挥部。

sentences.en: They are always doing it.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在这么做。

sentences.en: They always want to fight the Battle of Cannae.
sentences.zh: 他们总是想打坎尼会战。

sentences.en: And secondly, the reason I think the French have not anticipated this, and nobody has anticipated this,
sentences.zh: 其次，我认为法军没有预料到这一点，而且所有人都没有预料到这一点的原因是，

sentences.en: is because this is not an operation that would have been possible in the First World War, when you moved so much more slowly.
sentences.zh: 因为如果是在第一次世界大战那种推进速度慢得多的时期，这样的行动是根本不可能实现的。

sentences.en: It's only really possible because your panzers are game changers.
sentences.zh: 它之所以真正成为可能，是因为你们的装甲部队改变了游戏规则。

sentences.en: They can move so quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们的推进速度极快。

sentences.en: They can punch through an enemy line and get around you before you even know it.
sentences.zh: 他们能在你还没反应过来之前，就击穿敌军防线并绕到你身后。

sentences.en: But Guderian, who they know is in command, has written up this in Akhtung Panzer.
sentences.zh: 但大家都知道负责指挥的古德里安已经在《注意装甲》一书中写下了这些内容。

sentences.en: So why haven't they read it?
sentences.zh: 那他们为什么不读呢？

sentences.en: It's hopeless.
sentences.zh: 没救了。

sentences.en: They haven't done your level of research, or your brother's level of research, I should say.
sentences.zh: 他们没有做到你这个级别的研究，或者说，我应该说没有达到你弟弟的研究水平。

sentences.en: Clearly.
sentences.zh: 显然。

sentences.en: I mean, Tom, you look actually personally aggrieved that the French haven't been doing the reading.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，汤姆，看你的表情，好像法国人没做功课这件事让你觉得受到了个人冒犯一样。

sentences.en: Well, reading The War in the West, my brother's book, and listening to episodes on this in We Have Ways, his podcast,
sentences.zh: 好吧，读了《西方之战》——我弟弟的书，并听了在他的播客《我们有办法》中关于这部分的单集节目后，

sentences.en: I am left kind of stupefied by how hopeless the French are on this.
sentences.zh: 我对法国人在这一点上有多无可救药感到有点目瞪口呆。

sentences.en: And the British are complicit in as well, because they're not pointing it out either.
sentences.zh: 而且英国人也难辞其咎，因为他们也没有指出这一点。

sentences.en: No, it's poor from the British.
sentences.zh: 没错，英国人的表现也很糟糕。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So the date of the invasion was set for the early hours of Friday the 10th of May, as we've seen.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我们所见，入侵的日期定在了5月10日星期五的凌晨。

sentences.en: When the news broke in Berlin, the mood in Germany was very glum.
sentences.zh: 当消息传到柏林时，德国国内的气氛非常阴沉。

sentences.en: So in his diary, the American journalist William L.
sentences.zh: 因此，美国记者威廉·L·

sentences.en: Sherwin notes there's no crowds on the streets, and the people that he meets seem sunk in depression, because they think they're going to lose, you see.
sentences.zh: 夏伊勒在他的日记中记录道，街上空无一人，他遇到的人似乎都陷入了极度的沮丧，因为你看，他们觉得他们要输了。

sentences.en: Now, Hitler, at his rock eerie, the fell is a nest, he is very calm and confident.
sentences.zh: 现在，希特勒在他的岩石巢穴——狼穴里，显得非常冷静和自信。

sentences.en: And he says to his entourage, I think we'll beat France in six weeks, and then we'll find the British coming to talk to us, because they'll want to save their empire.
sentences.zh: 他对身边的人说，我想我们会在六周内击败法国，然后英国人就会来找我们谈判，因为他们想要保住他们的帝国。

sentences.en: So he's right about one of those prophecies and wrong about the second.
sentences.zh: 所以，他的这两个预言，一个猜对了，一个猜错了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And actually, as the first reports kind of come into the rock eerie, his optimism seems very well founded.
sentences.zh: 事实上，随着第一批消息传回狼穴，他的乐观态度似乎有着非常充分的依据。

sentences.en: So to begin with the Low Countries.
sentences.zh: 那么，先从低地国家说起。

sentences.en: At half four that morning, the German paratroopers and special forces had begun their operation.
sentences.zh: 那天凌晨四点半，德国伞兵和特种部队开始了他们的行动。

sentences.en: They'd been dropped by gliders and things.
sentences.zh: 他们是通过滑翔机之类的运送下去的。

sentences.en: They'd seized the key bridges and forts on the German and Dutch borders.
sentences.zh: 他们夺取了德荷边境上的关键桥梁和堡垒。

sentences.en: By mid-morning, so within hours, the Dutch are falling back to the north, and the German tanks are rolling through the fields of Holland.
sentences.zh: 到上午中段，也就是短短几小时内，荷兰军队向北撤退，德国坦克滚滚驶过荷兰的田野。

sentences.en: And the Dutch have no tanks, but they do have people on bicycles.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人虽然没有坦克，但他们有人骑自行车。

sentences.en: They do, but they're not very useful, as we will find out.
sentences.zh: 确实有，但正如我们随后会发现的，它们并没有什么用。

sentences.en: Now, the Allies have responded to this very sluggishly.
sentences.zh: 现在，盟军对这一情况的反应极其迟钝。

sentences.en: The French had heard rumours of a murmuring in the German lines a couple of days before,
sentences.zh: 法军在几天前就听到过德国防线有异动的传闻，

sentences.en: but their commanders said, no, there's always murmuring from the Germans, probably a false alarm.
sentences.zh: 但他们的指挥官说，不，德国人总是吵吵嚷嚷的，大概是虚惊一场吧。

sentences.en: The Allied Commander-in-Chief is a Frenchman, of course, because the French have by far the biggest troop contention.
sentences.zh: 盟军总司令自然是个法国人，因为法国拥有的军队兵力可以说是大得多。

sentences.en: He is General Maurice Gamelin.
sentences.zh: 他就是莫里斯·甘末林将军。

sentences.en: And he's a very, I think he's a very likable man in many ways, Gamelin.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得在很多方面，甘末林是个非常讨人喜欢的人。

sentences.en: He's kind of jaunty and jolly.
sentences.zh: 他总是兴高采烈、乐观开朗。

sentences.en: He loves art.
sentences.zh: 他热爱艺术。

sentences.en: He loves philosophy.
sentences.zh: 他热爱哲学。

sentences.en: He had been the protégé of our old friend, General Joffre, from 1914.
sentences.zh: 他曾是我们老朋友霞飞将军在1914年时的门生。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Loves a long lunch.
sentences.zh: 极其热爱漫长的午餐。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Long lunching.
sentences.zh: 午餐总是吃很久。

sentences.en: And imperturbable, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且泰然自若，不是吗？

sentences.en: And imperturbable, right?
sentences.zh: 而且总是沉着冷静，对吧？

sentences.en: And Gamelin has completely cut from the same cloth.
sentences.zh: 甘末林完全是同一个路数的人。

sentences.en: He says, listen, what I've learned from Joffre is you never lose your cool.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，我从霞飞身上学到的一点就是，你永远不要慌乱。

sentences.en: Things will probably be fine.
sentences.zh: 事情大概都会没问题的。

sentences.en: Don't overthink anything.
sentences.zh: 不要把任何事情想得太复杂。

sentences.en: You know, it'll be a long war.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这将是一场持久战。

sentences.en: Let's not stress about it.
sentences.zh: 咱们别为此感到压力山大。

sentences.en: The Germans attack.
sentences.zh: 德国人进攻了。

sentences.en: We shall advance calmly into Belgium to meet them.
sentences.zh: 我们要沉着地挺进比利时去迎接他们。

sentences.en: Of course, he doesn't know they're not going to come really through Belgium.
sentences.zh: 当然，他并不知道德国人根本不会真正通过比利时进攻。

sentences.en: So right from the start, the Allies are walking into the Germans' trap, just as Manstein and Hitler had dreamed.
sentences.zh: 所以从一开始，盟军就正步走入德国人的陷阱，正如曼施坦因和希特勒所梦想的那样。

sentences.en: Within four and a half days, the Germans have wiped the floor with the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 在四天半的时间里，德国人就把荷兰打得落花流水。

sentences.en: The climax coming on the 14th when the Luftwaffe bombed Rotterdam and they destroyed the old city of Rotterdam.
sentences.zh: 高潮出现在14日，当时德国空军轰炸了鹿特丹，摧毁了鹿特丹的老城区。

sentences.en: A massive story at the time.
sentences.zh: 这在当时是一件轰动性的大新闻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Apparently this was a mistake because the Dutch had already begun negotiating their surrender.
sentences.zh: 据说这是一个失误，因为荷兰人当时已经开始谈判投降了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so the orders went out to the bombers, you know, don't do it.
sentences.zh: 所以命令已经下达给轰炸机部队了，你知道的，让他们别炸。

sentences.en: But it was too late.
sentences.zh: 但已经太迟了。

sentences.en: The bombers had already left.
sentences.zh: 轰炸机已经出发了。

sentences.en: And so they, you know, as you say, they obliterate it.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，他们把那里夷为平地。

sentences.en: And actually, I mean, it works incredibly well for the Nazis, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的意思是，这对纳粹来说效果好得惊人，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it, again, it compounds this sense that there can be no opposition, that they are lethal.
sentences.zh: 因为这再次加深了一种印象：根本无法抵抗他们，他们是致命的。

sentences.en: And they have the Stukas, they kind of have a siren, don't they?
sentences.zh: 而且他们有斯图卡轰炸机，它们好像自带一种警报器，对吧？

sentences.en: So that when they drop, there's this terrifying kind of scream.
sentences.zh: 所以在它们俯冲时，会发出那种骇人的尖叫声。

sentences.en: And the whole thing is just, you know, this sense that there is no resisting the Nazi war machine.
sentences.zh: 整个过程给人的感觉就是，你知道的，纳粹战争机器是不可战胜的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: Even though, you know, it is quite an element of smoke and mirrors about it.
sentences.zh: 尽管这里面，你知道的，也有很大一部分是虚张声势的障眼法。

sentences.en: Well, in the case of Rotterdam, a lot of smoke.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就鹿特丹而言，可以说是烟雾弥漫。

sentences.en: Well, if you think the evasion starts on the 10th of May and what it must have been like to live through the next couple of weeks,
sentences.zh: 如果你想想5月10日战争爆发，以及经历接下来这几周会是怎样一种感受，

sentences.en: even if you're just following events in the newspapers, the sense of growing inevitability, of relentlessness, speed about the German advance.
sentences.zh: 哪怕你只是通过报纸关注局势，那种德国军队不断逼近的不可避免感、无情碾压感和神速，都历历在目。

sentences.en: So the Dutch surrender, four and a half days.
sentences.zh: 所以荷兰人在四天半内投降了。

sentences.en: The Queen, Vilhelmina, and her ministers escaped to London to become a government in exile.
sentences.zh: 威廉明娜女王和她的内阁逃往伦敦，成为了流亡政府。

sentences.en: The Belgians held out for 18 days, but they too were overwhelmed by sheer weight of numbers and firepower.
sentences.zh: 比利时人抵抗了18天，但他们同样被绝对优势的人数和火力给压垮了。

sentences.en: Interestingly, the Belgian king did not flee his country.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，比利时国王并没有逃离他的国家。

sentences.en: He had taken personal command of the army and he said, I don't want to desert them.
sentences.zh: 他亲自接管了军队的指挥权，并表示，我不想抛弃他们。

sentences.en: I should stay.
sentences.zh: 我应该留下来。

sentences.en: So he stays in Brussels.
sentences.zh: 所以他留在了布鲁塞尔。

sentences.en: He becomes a prisoner of the Germans and he was painted by the Allied press as a traitor.
sentences.zh: 他成了德国人的俘虏，但在盟军媒体的笔下，他被描绘成了一个叛徒。

sentences.en: The mirror, Daily Mirror, ran the headline about him.
sentences.zh: 《每日镜报》刊登了关于他的头条新闻。

sentences.en: I think a headline that no man wishes to read about himself.
sentences.zh: 我想这是一个任何男人都不希望看到别人用来形容自己的标题。

sentences.en: The face that every woman now despises.
sentences.zh: 一个现在被所有女性所鄙视的面孔。

sentences.en: What's the basis for that contempt?
sentences.zh: 这种蔑视的依据是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, it seems courageous that a commander in chief should stand.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，总司令选择坚守岗位似乎是一件很勇敢的事。

sentences.en: He was seen as a collaborator and actually the Belgians got rid of him after the war.
sentences.zh: 他被视为一个合作者，事实上战后比利时人也抛弃了他。

sentences.en: They saw him as tainted because he had not made the gestures of moral defiance, I guess, that King Christian had done in Denmark.
sentences.zh: 他们认为他身上有污点，因为他没有做出那种道德抵抗的姿态，我猜，就像丹麦的克里斯蒂安国王所做的那样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 原来如此。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think King Leopold had taken a very different approach.
sentences.zh: 我想利奥波德国王采取了截然不同的方法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: So within three weeks, both Holland and Belgium are under German military occupation where they will remain for the next five years.
sentences.zh: 因此在短短三周内，荷兰和比利时都落入了德国的军事占领之下，并且将在接下来的五年里一直如此。

sentences.en: But of course, this isn't where the main action is happening.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这并不是主要行动发生的地方。

sentences.en: This really is smoke and mirrors because the real action for the Germans is happening further south in the Ardennes foreSt.
sentences.zh: 这实际上只是障眼法，因为德国人的真正行动发生在更南边的阿登森林。

sentences.en: And here, you wanted numbers, Tom.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，你不是想要具体数字吗，汤姆。

sentences.en: Now, secretly, while I was talking, I was doing the maths.
sentences.zh: 刚才我在说话的时候，暗地里已经在心算这些数字了。

sentences.en: So here, General von Kleist, because I'm multitasking, he's leading 134,000 soldiers,
sentences.zh: 所以在这里，冯·克莱斯特将军——因为我在一心多用——正率领着134,000名士兵，

sentences.en: 1,200 tanks and 500 armoured vehicles through the kind of narrow roads that lead through the Ardennes foreSt.
sentences.zh: 1,200辆坦克以及500辆装甲车，沿着穿过阿登森林的狭窄道路前进。

sentences.en: And this means, surely, that they are now sitting ducks if the French air force attacks them.
sentences.zh: 这无疑意味着，如果法国空军对他们发动攻击，他们现在就是活靶子。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: Because there are only very few roads.
sentences.zh: 因为那里只有非常少的道路。

sentences.en: They're quite narrow.
sentences.zh: 它们相当狭窄。

sentences.en: Long tailbacks.
sentences.zh: 排起了长长的车队。

sentences.en: You know where they are.
sentences.zh: 你知道他们在哪儿。

sentences.en: Send the French planes in.
sentences.zh: 把法国飞机派过去吧。

sentences.en: But the French don't.
sentences.zh: 但法国人没有这么做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 这很像当年的情况，你知道的，就像普京进攻乌克兰时，基辅城外那种排着长队的俄军坦克之类的巨大交通拥堵一样。

sentences.en: It's the same story.
sentences.zh: 完全是同样的剧本。

sentences.en: The Germans said at the time it's the longest traffic jam in history.
sentences.zh: 德国人在当时说这是历史上最长的交通拥堵。

sentences.zh: 那是四列纵队，长达数百英里。

sentences.zh: 有坦克，是的，还有装甲车，但也有大车、马匹，以及你知道的，一排排的部队。

sentences.zh: 如果当时法国空军出动的话，战争早就结束了。

sentences.zh: 但他们没有。

sentences.zh: 他们接到命令，绝对不能停滞三天。

sentences.zh: 为了让他们保持清醒，还给他们发了兴奋剂。

sentences.zh: 你必须一鼓作气坚持三天。

sentences.en: Can't stop.
sentences.zh: 不能停下。

sentences.en: Without having been destroyed from above by the French.
sentences.zh: 在没有遭到法国人从空中毁灭性打击的情况下。

sentences.zh: 现在，当他们到达河流时，这是一个关键时刻。

sentences.zh: 如果法军能够在河边挡住他们，那么镰刀收割计划就破产了。
